senses.sense_definition: beter zijn dan verwacht; minder erg of moeilijk zijn dan men dacht

examples.text: De resultaten <w>vielen mee</w>, gezien de moeilijke omstandigheden van het afgelopen jaar.

target_lang_translations.en: The results <w>were better than expected</w>, given the difficult circumstances of the past year.

examples.text: Ik dacht dat het examen heel lastig zou zijn, maar het <w>viel</w> gelukkig erg <w>mee</w>.

target_lang_translations.en: I thought the exam would be very difficult, but fortunately it <w>wasn't as bad as expected</w> at all.

target_lang_definitions.en: to be better than expected; to be less difficult or bad than anticipated

en.target_lang_sense_clarification: when a result or situation is more positive than anticipated
to result in a more favorable way than one thought

en.target_lang_word: not be as bad as expected
en.target_lang_sense_clarification: when a difficult task or negative situation is easier to handle than feared

senses.sense_definition: samen met iets anders naar beneden vallen

examples.text: De bomen <w>vielen</w> met de lawine <w>mee</w> het diepe dal in.

target_lang_translations.en: The trees <w>fell along</w> with the avalanche into the deep valley.

examples.text: Toen de muur instortte, <w>vielen</w> de schilderijen ook direct <w>mee</w> naar de grond.

target_lang_translations.en: When the wall collapsed, the paintings also immediately <w>fell down with</w> it to the ground.

target_lang_definitions.en: to fall down together with something else

en.target_lang_sense_clarification: to drop or tumble down at the same time as another object
to be carried down by something else that is falling
